checks.note: It names the default `cart=[]` as the cause and says it is created once, when the function is defined.
It says every call without a `cart` reuses the same list, so items pile up, and shows the second call returning 12.
The fix uses `cart=None` with `if cart is None: cart = []`, the standard idiom.
Only the default value changes and a two-line guard is added. The append and sum lines are untouched.
The explanation is correct and short, and the expected outputs (2 and 10) are right.
